subject: Social Habits
title: Doing things by myself
objectives: Children will do simple self-help tasks with less help.
Children will say "I can do it".
content: Putting on shoes and bag, washing and drying hands, and packing away and helping.
teachingActivities: Allow time; wait before helping; give just enough help; praise effort ("You did it yourself"); use real shoes, bags and jackets; set up a dress-up area; avoid taking over when a child struggles; link to routines at arrival and home time.
learnerActivities: Do simple self-help tasks with less help and say "I can do it".
resources: Shoes with Velcro and with laces for practice
assessment: Observe whether each child does one self-help task with little support and says "I can do it".
expectedOutcomes: Does one self-help task with little support.

lessons.title: Shoes and bag
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will put on shoes and a bag with less help.
successCriteria: Puts on shoes with Velcro with little help
Puts a bag on their back
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt many habits and helped at home and school.
lessons.starter: Show a pair of shoes and say "We can put on our shoes by ourselves."
teacherActivities: Show how to put the right shoe on the right foot and close the Velcro.
Let each child try with their own shoes.
Show how to put a bag on both shoulders.
learnerActivities: Children repeat I can do it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to put the right shoe on the right foot and close the Velcro. Children: Children watch and copy.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child try with their own shoes. Children: Child puts on shoes.
Step 3. Teacher: Show how to put a bag on both shoulders. Children: Child puts on a bag.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "I can do it." Children: Children repeat I can do it.

practical.title: Shoes and bag
practical.safety: Wait before helping and keep floors clear of tripping hazards. Help gently and never rush children.

differentiation.support: Help with the first step and let the child do the rest.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to help a friend with Velcro.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Puts on shoes with little help
lessons.conclusion: Stand up and say "I did it."
lessons.homeConnection: Give your child time to put on shoes and a bag by themselves.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "put on shoes and a bag with less help" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: I can do it, I can do it myself.

lessons.title: Washing and drying by myself
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will wash and dry their hands with little help.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt many habits and helped at home and school.
lessons.starter: Show clean hands and say "We can wash our hands by ourselves."
teacherActivities: Remind children of the steps: wet, soap, rub, rinse and dry.
Watch each child wash with a song.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Remind children of the steps: wet, soap, rub, rinse and dry. Children: Children say the steps.
Step 2. Teacher: Watch each child wash with a song. Children: Child washes with the song.
Step 3. Teacher: Help only where needed. Children: Child dries hands.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "I did it myself." Children: Children say I did it.

practical.title: Wash by myself
practical.safety: Supervise closely and wipe spills at once. Use mild soap and a safe step stool.

differentiation.support: Wash together and name each step.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say the steps to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Show clean hands and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child wash hands independently while you watch.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "wash and dry their hands with little help" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Packing away and helping

resources: A bag with a bottle and a cloth
lessons.starter: Show a bag and say "At home time we pack our bags ourselves."
teacherActivities: Show how to put a bottle and a cloth in the bag.
Let children pack their own bags.
Sing the tidy song and put toys away.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to put a bottle and a cloth in the bag. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children pack their own bags. Children: Child packs a bag.
Step 3. Teacher: Sing the tidy song and put toys away. Children: Children tidy up.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "I helped pack away." Children: Children say I helped.

practical.title: Pack and tidy

differentiation.support: Pack together and name each item.

lessons.title: Dressing up
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will practise putting on and taking off clothing in play.
successCriteria: Puts on a jacket or hat
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt many habits and helped at home and school.
resources: Dress-up clothes with big buttons or Velcro
lessons.starter: Show a box of dress-up clothes and say "Let us put on our clothes by ourselves."
teacherActivities: Show how to put on a jacket and do up Velcro.
Let each child choose and put on a piece of clothing.
Look in the mirror and say "I did it."
Take off the clothing and put it away.
learnerActivities: Child puts the clothing in the basket.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to put on a jacket and do up Velcro. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child choose and put on a piece of clothing. Children: Child dresses up.
Step 3. Teacher: Look in the mirror and say "I did it." Children: Child looks in the mirror.
Step 4. Teacher: Take off the clothing and put it away. Children: Child puts the clothing in the basket.

practical.title: Dress-up play
steps: Take it off and put it away.
practical.safety: Use clean clothes only and avoid anything with cords or ties around necks. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Hold the sleeve and let the child push their arm through.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to help a friend with a button or Velcro.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Puts on and takes off clothing
lessons.conclusion: Tidy the dress-up box and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Encourage your child to dress themselves with time and patience.

lessons.title: Week 9 independence check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child manages self-help tasks.
successCriteria: Does a self-help task with little support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt many habits and helped at home and school.
lessons.starter: Sing the I can do it song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: shoes and bag, washing and packing.
At each station watch how the child manages.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: shoes and bag, washing and packing. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child manages. Children: Child tries with little help.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Independence stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station closely and wipe spills at once. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show a friend how to do a task.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: puts on shoes; washes and dries hands; packs a bag; says I can do it.

questions.question: What can you do by yourself?
questions.expected: Wash hands or put on shoes.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep letting your child do things for themselves.
